name: Mono-compatible wide bass: strip the fundamental from a unison wavetable (FFT/harmonic editor), keep the wide upper harmonics with unison, then add a separate mono sine as the fundamental with phase-randomize at 0
goal: Keep a wide Reese-style bass powerful in mono and easier to phase-align with the kick: remove the first harmonic (fundamental) from the unison oscillator so unison only widens the overtones, then restore power with a second oscillator that is a clean sine (no unison). Delta vs bass cluster / kick-bass-four-level-lock: the fundamental is edited out of the wavetable itself before unison, rather than only EQ-splitting a full-spectrum voice into sub vs mid after the fact; also shows why zeroing phase-random on a normal unison Reese creates a laser-sweep artifact, so the clean sine must be the separate voice.

source.title: How to make any "WIDE BASS" mono-compatible!

prerequisites: Any wavetable synth with a harmonic/FFT editor (or an equivalent way to zero the fundamental bin), unison, a second oscillator, and phase-randomize / free-run phase control
Optional oscilloscope and a mono-fold utility

inputs.name: bass_midi
inputs.description: Bass part (often for a drop or sustained root)

outputs.name: mono_safe_wide_bass
outputs.description: Wide mid-bass with a stable mono fundamental

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Do not put unison or phase randomization on the sine fundamental.
Verify in mono fold-down: power must stay steady, not pump.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.
Steady pitch: leave out intentional pitch-drift LFOs unless the brief asks for tape wobble (Matt prefers steady pitch).

steps.action: Start from a saw (or similarly bright) wavetable. Optionally add a gentle low-pass so the raw tone is easier on the ears.
Open the wavetable / FFT / harmonic editor. Identify the first harmonic (fundamental) and remove or zero it so the table is overtones only. Solo A/B: the tone should sound thinner and weaker.
Enable unison on that weakened oscillator (e.g. 5 voices) with a small detune (source default ~0.25). This widens only the overtones.
Enable a second oscillator as a pure sine at the same pitch. Leave its unison off. This sine is the new fundamental.
steps.expect: Full power returns; fundamental is mono

steps.action: Set the sine oscillator's phase-randomize / rand to 0 so every note starts at the same phase (stable for kick alignment). Do not zero rand on a normal full-spectrum unison Reese — that creates a sweeping laser artifact and still collapses in mono.
steps.expect: Consistent note-on phase on the sub only

steps.action: A/B the patch in mono: the fundamental-stripped+sine version keeps power; a normal unison Reese pumps and thins. Optionally check an oscilloscope against the kick.

verification: Mono fold-down keeps roughly the same power as stereo (no pumping).
Unison is audible as width in the mids/highs only.
Sine fundamental has fixed start phase; no laser-sweep artifact.
